nodes.characterization_summary: CoOOH XRD patterns match heterogenite with no phase changes; Ni3Fe1Sx shows no detectable phase changes (Figure S1, S8).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffractograms of the catalysts are provided in Supporting Information... Section 1 and Figure S1... XRD patterns recorded for CoOOH after voltammetric cycling in 1 M KOH without and with 0.6MNaCl present were essentially identical and matched the tabulated data for heterogenite; no detectable phase changes were found for Ni3Fe1Sx as well (Figure S8).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows no noteworthy changes in transition metal 2p, O 1s, S 2p and survey spectra for CoOOH and Ni3Fe1Sx; no Cl detected after activation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS analysis produced similar outcomes, i.e., no noteworthy changes in the transition metal 2p, O 1s, S 2p and overall survey spectra (Figures S11-S12). ... no Cl could be detected by XPS after the activation.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS shows ca. 1.5 at.% Co leached from CoOOH, 4.8 at.% Ni and 13 at.% Fe from Ni3Fe1Sx after activation; Ni/Fe/Co contaminants in electrolyte below detection limit.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP-MS analysis of 1M KOH + 0.6M NaCl before and after activation showed that ca. 1.5 at.% of Co leached from CoOOH into the electrolyte solution, while Ni3Fe1Sx lost ca. 4.8 at.% of Ni and ca. 13 at.% of Fe (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals roughening of the surface and development of numerous pits for both CoOOH and Ni3Fe1Sx after cycling in 1 M KOH + 0.6 M NaCl but not in chloride-free 1 M KOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The only physical characterization techniques that revealed changes in CoOOH and Ni3Fe1Sx induced by saline-alkaline activation were SEM and TEM. Specifically, roughening of the surface and development of numerous pits were observed for both catalytic materials after cycling in 1M KOH +0.6M NaCl but not in chloride-free 1M KOH (Figures 3a,b; S13 and S14).

nodes.characterization_summary: (Pseudo)capacitance Cp increases by factor of 1.62 ± 0.01 for CoOOH and 1.60 ± 0.01 for Ni3Fe1Sx after saline-alkaline activation (Figures S15-S16).
nodes.evidence_snippet: To test if this partial corrosion induced an increase in the electrochemically active surface area, (pseudo)capacitance (Cp) measurements were conducted (Figures S15-S16). It was found that activation in a saline-alkaline solution increases the Cp values by a factor of 1.62 ± 0.01 and 1.60 ± 0.01 for CoOOH and Ni3Fe1Sx, respectively (Figure 3c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Density of electrochemically active Co and NiFe sites Γ increases (3.2 ± 0.1)-fold for CoOOH and (3.5 ± 0.1)-fold for Ni3Fe1Sx, calculated from Co/Ni reduction peak charges (Figure S18).
nodes.evidence_snippet: We analyzed the density of electrochemically active cobalt and nickel-iron sites (Γ) by applying Faraday's law to the charges associated with the Co(3.7+δ)/3+ and Ni(3+δ)/2+ voltammetric reduction peaks... this increase was approximately the same as the observed increase in the mass-normalized catalytic activity... viz., (3.2 ± 0.1)-fold for CoOOH and (3.5 ± 0.1)-fold for Ni3Fe1Sx (Figure 3d).
